newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps mostly dip, fuel down $1, CFDs steady.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps mostly dip, fuel down $1, CFDs steady.

text.p: European oil swaps were mostly slightly lower on Wednesday morning in thin trading conditions.
Gasoline fell $1.50 a tonne for May swaps after trading at $190.50 and $191 for physical about $3 below Tuesday levels.
Gasoline crack spreads against Brent were well bid with June at $4.95 a barrel and the third and fourth quarters were pegged around $4.10 and $3.10 respectively.
Gas oil against Brent held steady at $4.35 a barrel on the third quarter and $4.85 on the fourth.

Heavy fuel eased $1 a tonne to $82 for May and $87 for low sulphur. Dealers said the market remains bearish in Europe but further losses were unlikely due to firm levels in Singapore where May was pegged around $97.50 earlier on Wednesday.
Brent CFDs were broadly stable at 62 cents under June for next weeks dates. Dealers said a lack of buying had stalled physical crude markets but premiums had held steady.
Wet Brent remained around 48 cents under May or the equivalent of 76 cents under June. -- Sam Arnold-Forster, London Newsroom +44 171 542 4984
